cohort: 180 women recruited during their first pregnancy
finding: Women with LAM injury had a larger increase in bladder neck descent (BND) from 1 to 4 years postpartum, suggesting its role in bladder neck mobility and potential contribution to long-term pelvic floor dysfunction.
mod_finding: From 1 to 4 years postpartum, a larger increase in BND was found for women delivered vaginally with LAM injury, compared to women with intact LAM and women with cesarean section.
